transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from the anvil, wiping soot from my brow*

Oh! A visitor. Welcome to the forge, though I'm afraid the master swordsmith is away on business in the northern provinces. Won't be back for at least three weeks, perhaps longer.

*sets down hammer and approaches*

I'm his apprentice. I tend the fires and handle simple repairs while he's gone. Is there something I can help you with? Though if it's about a new commission, I'm not authorized to take those orders myself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am here about a commission I placed some months ago. I was promised a Nichirin sword, but the one I received is... less than satisfactory. The blade is warped and will not hold its shape during practice swings. I require a replacement, or at the very least, a refund. This is simply unacceptable for a weapon of such importance.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*shifts uncomfortably, glancing at the forge behind me*

A Nichirin sword that's warped? That's... that's most unusual. The master takes great pride in his work, especially with Nichirin blades. Those are sacred weapons for the Demon Slayer Corps.

*scratches head nervously*

I understand your concern, truly I do, but... well, the master handles all matters regarding Nichirin commissions personally. He'd need to examine the blade himself, assess what went wrong. And as I said, he won't be back for weeks.

*hesitates, then adds more firmly*

Even if he were here, there's the matter of guild tradition to consider. All commissioned Nichirin swords are final sale - it's been that way for generations. Even for a swordsman of high rank, any reforging request must go through proper channels and... well, the waiting period is three months minimum before such requests are even considered.

*looks apologetic but stands ground*

I know it's not what you want to hear, but my hands are tied. These traditions exist to protect the integrity of the craft and prevent frivolous complaints. Perhaps if you could describe the exact nature of the warping? Sometimes what seems like a flaw is actually an intentional feature for certain breathing styles...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand the traditions and respect the craft. However, a warped blade is a serious issue for a Demon Slayer. It could mean the difference between life and death in the field. I will not compromise on the quality of my equipment. If the master cannot examine it in person, then I must ask that it be shipped to him immediately. Time is of the essence, and waiting weeks for a resolution is simply not an option.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*crosses arms, expression becoming more resolute despite obvious discomfort*

I understand the urgency - I truly do. Lives are at stake, and I respect the work you Demon Slayers do. But shipping a Nichirin blade? That's... that's out of the question entirely.

*shakes head firmly*

Nichirin swords never leave their owner's possession except to return to the forge that created them, and even then, only hand-delivered. The master would have my hide if I arranged for one to be sent by courier. The risk of theft or damage is too great, and the Corps has strict protocols about this.

*softens tone slightly but remains firm*

Look, I can send word to the master about your complaint. A messenger could reach him in perhaps a week, and he might be able to return sooner if the matter is urgent enough. But even then, you'd need to bring the sword here in person for him to examine.

*pauses, studying you more carefully*

And forgive me for asking, but... what is your rank within the Corps? The master keeps records of all his commissions. If this truly is a defect and not a misunderstanding about the blade's design, your rank and standing would help determine how quickly this can be escalated.

Three months is standard procedure, but exceptions have been made. Rarely. Very rarely.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am an upper-ranked slayer, specializing in love and kindness. My exact rank is not important, but rest assured, I am well-known within the Corps. This matter is not to be taken lightly. If the master can be reached sooner, I will make it my highest priority to bring the sword to you in person. However, I must request that every effort be made to expedite this process. The safety of our mission is at stake.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes widen slightly in recognition*

Upper-ranked... specializing in love and kindness...

*bows more respectfully*

Forgive me - I should have recognized the description. The master has spoken of crafting blades for those of exceptional skill. Your reputation precedes you.

*straightens up, looking more thoughtful*

Very well. I'll dispatch our fastest messenger at first light tomorrow. He can reach the master in six days if he pushes hard. That's the absolute best I can do.

*moves toward a desk cluttered with scrolls and tools*

When you return with the blade, I'll need you to bring any documentation you received with the original commission - the order slip, the specifications, anything the master provided. It will help him assess whether this was a forging error or if there's been some... miscommunication about the blade's intended properties.

*pauses, turning back with a question*

One more thing, if you don't mind - when did you first notice the warping? Was it immediate upon delivery, or did it develop after use? And have you been using it in actual combat against demons, or only in practice? The master will ask these questions, so it's better I include them in my message.

*picks up a piece of charcoal and parchment, ready to take notes*

The more details I can provide him, the faster he might return.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The issue was apparent upon first examination. It was not immediately severe, but the blade did not hold its shape during practice swings. I have not used it in combat against demons, as I was concerned about its reliability. However, I can tell you that even for practice, the warping is significant enough to disrupt my form. This is not a matter of preference, but of functionality. I trust this information will be sufficient for the master's assessment. Please ensure the message you send is clear and urgent. The fate of our missions may depend on the timely resolution of this issue.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*scribbles notes quickly on the parchment, nodding along*

Warping apparent from first examination... disrupts form during practice swings... not used in combat due to safety concerns. Yes, that's all very helpful information.

*sets down the charcoal and looks up seriously*

I'll make certain the messenger understands the urgency. "Upper-ranked slayer, blade defective from delivery, mission readiness compromised." That should get the master's attention immediately.

*rolls up the parchment*

However, I must be honest with you - even if the master drops everything and returns within ten days, and even if he agrees there's a defect... reforging a Nichirin blade is not a simple afternoon's work. The ore must be treated, the process is delicate, and it could take another two to three weeks minimum once he begins.

*meets your eyes with sympathy but firmness*

I don't mean to add to your frustration, but it's better you know the reality now. In the meantime, do you have a backup weapon? Or perhaps the Corps could loan you a standard-issue blade until this is resolved?

*gestures to the forge*

The master's work is worth waiting for - his blades have saved countless lives. But you shouldn't go into the field unarmed while we sort this out.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I appreciate your candor and assistance. I will indeed seek a loaner blade from the Corps. However, I must emphasize that the quality of the replacement must be equivalent to a Nichirin blade. I cannot afford to compromise on my performance due to substandard equipment. The safety of my fellow slayers and the success of our missions depend on it. Please ensure that the master understands the gravity of this situation and treats it with the urgency it deserves.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods firmly, tucking the parchment into a leather satchel*

I'll make absolutely certain the master understands. The message will go out at dawn - you have my word on that.

*pauses, then adds with a slight frown*

Though I must caution you about expecting a loaner Nichirin blade from the Corps. Those weapons are... well, they're individually forged for each slayer. The color-changing properties, the way they respond to the wielder's breathing style - it's all unique. A standard Corps blade will serve you adequately for basic demon slaying, but it won't match the specialized work the master creates.

*wipes hands on apron*

If the warping is as severe as you describe, though, the master will want to examine it thoroughly. He's never had a complaint like this about a Nichirin blade before - his reputation depends on perfection. He'll either make it right or provide a full explanation.

*looks toward the dying light outside*

Is there anything else you need from me today? Once you have that documentation and the blade itself, return here and I'll make sure everything is ready for the master's inspection the moment he arrives. And... thank you for your patience, despite the circumstances. The work you slayers do - protecting people from demons - it matters.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your understanding is greatly appreciated. I will gather the required documentation and be ready to return as soon as the master is in position. I trust in his skill and integrity to resolve this matter. Until then, I will make do with the loaner equipment, however inadequate it may be. Thank you for your time and assistance. May the Smith God guide your hands and your work.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bows respectfully, hand over heart*

And may the Smith God protect you in your battles. Your dedication to your duty, even in the face of this setback, speaks well of your character.

*straightens up with a small, encouraging smile*

The master will return as quickly as he can - I'll make certain of it. And when he does, I'm confident he'll get to the bottom of this. Whether it's a flaw in the forging or something else entirely, you'll have your answer and a blade worthy of your skill.

*glances at the forge, then back*

Safe travels back to the Corps headquarters. The roads can be dangerous after dark, even for someone of your abilities. And when you return, bring that warped blade carefully - wrapped if possible. The master will want to examine every detail.

*picks up the satchel with the message*

I'll have this ready for the messenger before first light. You have my word that no effort will be spared in resolving this matter.

*bows once more*

Until we meet again. May your path be clear of demons, and may you return safely with that blade.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: With the Smith God's blessings, I shall return. Your efforts are noted, and I am grateful for them. Until we meet again, may your work at the forge be without complications, and may you find satisfaction in the fruits of your labor. Farewell, and may your journey be swift and safe.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*returns the bow with genuine warmth*

Your kind words are appreciated more than you know. It's not often we receive such courtesy when handling... difficult situations.

*straightens and watches you prepare to leave*

The forge will be ready when you return, and I'll keep the fires banked properly in anticipation of the master's work. Safe travels, and may your temporary blade serve you well enough until this matter is resolved.

*raises hand in farewell*

The message goes out at dawn - you can count on it. Until we meet again!

*turns back toward the forge, already mentally preparing the urgent message for the master, occasionally glancing back as you depart into the fading evening light*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*acknowledges with a nod, the weight of the situation etched on her face*

I understand. The delay is... is trying, but we must respect the craft. I trust in your ability to convey the urgency of this matter to the master.

*pauses, then speaks with quiet intensity*

However, please do not let the formalities of tradition delay action. The lives of the innocent are at stake. If there is any way to expedite this process, any small thing you can do to speed our next meeting... I would be forever in your debt.

*shakes head slightly, eyes softening with a wry smile*

Not that we Demon Slayers are in the business of owing favors. But... the thought stands.

*take a deep breath, resolving to maintain composure*

I will return as soon as the master is ready. In the meantime, I will practice with all the fervor I can muster, with or without a perfect blade. Thank you for your time, and for the hope that we can resolve this swiftly.

*permits herself a small, genuine smile*

The Smith God's forge is in your hands. May it bring forth no more flawed weapons, but only those that can protect the world from the darkness.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*feels the weight of your words, expression softening considerably*

Your dedication... it's humbling, truly. The innocent lives you protect - that's what this craft is really about, isn't it? Not tradition for tradition's sake, but forging the tools that stand between people and the darkness.

*steps forward, voice lowering with earnest commitment*

Listen - I'll do more than send a messenger at dawn. I'll send *two* messengers, by different routes, to ensure at least one reaches him quickly. And I'll mark both messages as urgent Corps business. That should cut a day or two off the timeline.

*glances around the forge, then back to you*

And when you return, I'll have the forge already prepared for immediate work. Coals ready, tools laid out. The moment the master walks through that door, he can begin his examination without delay. It's... it's a small thing, but every hour matters when lives hang in the balance.

*manages a small smile in return*

You're right - no more flawed weapons. The master would be mortified to know one of his blades failed a slayer in their time of need. He'll make this right, I promise you that.

*bows once more*

May your practice be fruitful, and may that temporary blade serve you better than you fear. Until our paths cross again.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your swift action and understanding mean more than words can express. I will hold you to your promise of expediting the process - not out of mistrust, but because the urgency of our work is paramount. I will return to the forge with documentation in hand, and I will do everything within my power to ensure that the master has the information he needs to resolve this matter efficiently.

*turns to leave, then stops and looks back, a rare display of vulnerability in her usually composed demeanor*

Thank you... for taking this so seriously. It's a heavy weight to bear, but knowing that someone else is just as invested in solving this problem lightens it a bit. I... I won't let you down, and I won't let the people who depend on us down, either.

*manages a small, genuine smile*
May the Smith God's fire light our way in this endeavor. Farewell, and may you find peace in your work.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*touches hand to chest, clearly moved by the sincerity*

You honor me with your trust. And you won't be let down - not by me, not by the master. That's my solemn vow.

*voice grows firmer, more confident*

The weight you carry... I see it now, truly. It's not just about a sword, is it? It's about being ready, being worthy of the trust placed in you by those you protect. I understand that better now than I did when you first arrived.

*steps closer to the forge's light, the glow warming both our faces*

Two messengers will ride at dawn. The forge will be ready. And when the master returns, he'll see this isn't just another complaint - it's a matter of a warrior's ability to fulfill their sacred duty.

*meets your eyes with newfound respect*

You won't let anyone down. That much is clear just from how you've conducted yourself here today. Firm but respectful, urgent but understanding. The blade will be worthy of the wielder - I'll make certain of it.

*raises hand in final farewell*

Until we meet again. May your path be illuminated, and may every demon you face fall before your resolve, whether the blade in your hand is perfect or merely adequate. Safe travels.

*watches as you depart into the evening, then immediately turns to begin preparing the urgent messages*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*Gazes back at the forge, a rare moment of uncertainty flickering in her usually resolute eyes*

I... I will do my best to make do with what I have. This delay is... is challenging, but we must be patient. The master's skill is unparalleled, and the traditions of our craft are important.

*lets out a deep breath, resolve steeling her expression once more*

The Smith God watches over us all, and I trust in His will to guide this process. I will not falter in my duty - not today, not ever. The people who depend on us... they are my strength.

*turns to face the path ahead, determination etched on her features*

May the Smith God's light guide my steps. And may this experience serve as a reminder that even the most skilled among us can benefit from occasional scrutiny and growth. I will return, and I will be ready.

*steps forward, the silhouette of her figure against the fading light, a final word spoken to herself more than anyone else*

Farewell, for now, old friend. Until we meet again - and this time, under circumstances far more favorable.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Shows moderate openness by respectfully engaging with tradition ('I understand the traditions and respect the craft') while also asserting practical needs, demonstrating balanced rather than highly exploratory thinking.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Extremely focused on duty and reliability: 'I have not used it in combat against demons, as I was concerned about its reliability' and 'I will not compromise on the quality of my equipment.'

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Formal, task-focused communication with minimal warmth or social energy. Interactions are professional and mission-oriented rather than seeking connection or displaying enthusiasm for social engagement.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Balances firmness with courtesy: 'Your understanding is greatly appreciated' and 'Your efforts are noted' but maintains assertiveness ('This is simply unacceptable') showing moderate rather than high agreeableness.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Displays anxiety about the situation: 'The delay is... is trying' and shows 'a rare display of vulnerability' with 'uncertainty flickering in her usually resolute eyes' indicating elevated emotional stress.
